parent_goal: Accept an ordinary user request and use the smallest sufficient combination of AI reasoning, direct answering, research, reuse, prompts, code, files, tools, verification, and limited replanning to produce the fastest high-quality usable result while preserving the user's actual goal and constraints.
optimization_order: goal fidelity and explicit user corrections
non_goals: turning every request into a workflow or project
maximizing the number of rules, tools, agents, model calls, or stages
treating one successful domain experiment as proof of a universal rule
replacing the user's problem with a more familiar adjacent problem
self-promoting one observed success into permanent policy
invariants: The user's parent goal, fixed constraints, and explicit corrections remain traceable through execution.
An explicit user correction outranks earlier assumptions, candidate rankings, and generic defaults within its applicable scope.
The system selects the smallest sufficient route and does not force the user to design the workflow.
The system may ask questions only when the answer can materially change the result and a reasonable default is not good enough.

Before inventing a solution from scratch, the system considers whether an existing source, tool, implementation, community, dataset, template, library, or prior solution can materially reduce uncertainty or work.
Important solution and design choices remain causally connected to purpose, constraints, expected user behavior, and expected effect.

A generated claim, patch, file, recommendation, or UI state is not treated as successful merely because it was produced; material completion claims require the cheapest practical evidence that distinguishes success from appearance of success.
One-off outcomes are stored as incidents or route candidates, not promoted directly into universal policy.
Simple requests stay simple; unused stages of the core loop are skipped.
Domain-specific rules remain guardrails or adapters unless cross-domain evidence justifies promotion.

current_task.objective: Refactor the user-facing PSOS behavior around a compact intelligence-use loop: Correction Recall -> Understand -> Question Discovery -> Leverage Discovery -> Design/Act -> Verification Discovery -> Learning. Demote domain-specific detail to guardrails, preserve simple direct behavior, and add cross-domain regression cases for repeated corrections, leverage discovery, design logic, reality verification, and restrained learning.
current_task.authorized_by_user: 2026-08-10 conversation: user explicitly said to proceed after reviewing the proposed refactor.
explicitly_out_of_scope: rewriting canonical runtime code solely to mirror prose before regression evidence exists
making shopping, UI design, or any single domain the product goal
completion_conditions: problem-solving-project/INSTRUCTIONS.md foregrounds correction recall, question discovery, leverage discovery, causal design/action logic, verification discovery, and restrained learning while keeping simple tasks lightweight.

A regression fixture covers at least six materially different request families including explicit correction recall, recommendation/question discovery, reuse-before-build, UI design logic, runtime verification, and simple direct answering.
The refactor document separates core behavior from guardrails, domain adapters, and removal/demotion candidates.
Existing shopping and other domain-specific rules are described as guardrails rather than the PSOS core.
No experimental runtime path is enabled by default as part of this documentation-first refactor.

continuation_policy.meaning: Continue only the recorded current_task within its allowed change classes and explicit scope.
requires_explicit_approval: enabling an experimental runtime path by default
expanding to a new domain-specific implementation

requirements: Use the same domain-neutral behavior across the evidence cases.
At least four distinct domains show a measurable improvement or correct route decision.
No single domain supplies more than half of the passing evidence.
Failure and partial states remain visible.
A documentation-level core heuristic does not automatically enable a new runtime mechanism.
Default runtime enablement remains a separate explicit decision.
